lead_story.topic: Michigan survives Western Michigan with controversial clock management — refs add 1 second, Hail Mary wins it, Michigan storms field
lead_story.headline: Michigan Gets the Call

tweets.text:
RIGGED 

Ball in the air and the clock is very CLEARLY at ZERO! Yet the referees added 1 second for Michigan leading to a walk-off Hail Mary win. 

INSANE
That was the worst incident involving a timer in Michigan history and Ted Kaczynski went there

The Big Ten made a statement regarding the controversial ending of Western Michigan-Michigan.

(via @bigten)

lead_story.research_notes: MASSIVE STORY OVERRIDE — this is the robbery the entire sports internet is talking about. Western Michigan was 28-point underdog, led 13-10, clock showed 0:00 before ball hit defender's hands on incomplete pass, refs reviewed and added 1 second back, Bryce Underwood threw Hail Mary TD to JJ Buchanan on next play, Michigan won 13-10, then STORMED THE FIELD against a MAC opponent they were favored by 28 over. The optics are catastrophic: Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham admitted to WMU coach 'there wasn't time' per HaterReport video. AlbertBreer called the angle 'gotta be CLEAR to overturn, this seems 55/45 at best.' PFTCommenter: 'worst incident involving a timer in Michigan history and Ted Kaczynski went there.' The Big Ten released a statement defending the call, which only makes it worse. Compare this to the greatest upsets in MAC history — Western Michigan beating #4 Wisconsin in 2016, Toledo nearly upsetting Michigan State yesterday (Day 1 of this story log). A MAC team upsetting a top-10 Big Ten team is legendary; having it stolen on a 1-second review is a travesty. Research: what are the most controversial clock decisions in CFB history? The 2013 Iron Bowl? The 2016 Michigan-Ohio State spot? This is now in that tier. The internet's reaction is universal condemnation: BarstoolBigCat, PFTCommenter, HaterReport, NFLMemes, BillBarnwell, KevinOConnor, ghetto_gronk all called it a robbery. Michigan storming the field is the cherry on top — you storm when you WIN an upset, not when you escape one via ref intervention. The memes write themselves: refs walking into Michigan locker room to pick up checks, refs as Michigan's 12th man, etc. This is the lead because it's the biggest story of the weekend AND because it fits MASSIVE STORY OVERRIDE: a truly controversial call that the entire sports world is reacting to, with memes, outrage, and disbelief flooding every corner of the internet.
lead_story.gif_concept: Smug satisfaction at getting away with something you absolutely did not deserve — the vibe when you know you got bailed out and you're just gonna grin and take it
lead_story.meme_concept: Michigan and the refs tonight — they are functionally the same, mirror-image parties working together, both claiming they're just doing their job

beats.angle: The clock controversy itself — what the video shows, what the Big Ten said, what the internet saw
beats.landing: Reader understands this was not 'clear and obvious' and the rule requires it to be

beats.angle: The Hail Mary itself and Michigan storming the field — against a MAC team they were favored by 28 over
beats.landing: The absurdity of the celebration lands as the punchline, not just the controversial call

beats.angle: The Michigan coach admitting there wasn't time, the Big Ten's statement, the internet's universal condemnation
beats.landing: Even Michigan knows they got away with one, and the cover-up makes it worse

supporting_stories.topic: Roger Goodell extended as NFL commissioner through 2030 season — will serve 24 years, until age 72
supporting_stories.headline: Goodell's Got Four More Years

tweets.text: NFL teams were notified today that commissioner Roger Goodell now has finalized a new four-season extension that runs through the 2030 league season. The contract expires March 31, 2031.

NFL teams received the following memo from Robert Kraft and Compensation Committee, announcing Roger Goodell’s new extension through the 2030 season. 
 
As members of the Compensation Committee, we’re pleased to announce that we have reached agreement with Roger to remain as Commissioner through the 2030 League Season, ending on March 31, 2031. 
 
Throughout the negotiation process, the Committee worked closely with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure a deal that aligns Roger’s compensation with the League’s long-term interests and success.  To that end, the agreement is heavily performance based, with more than 95% of the total compensation tied to Roger’s and the NFL’s performance measured against various metrics and at the discretion of the Compensation Committee. 
 
We believe we are very fortunate to have Roger at the helm for the next four years.
 
If any of you has any questions, please reach out to any of us.
 
Robert Kraft (Chairman)
John Mara
Shad Khan
Jimmy Haslam
Michael Bidwill
Greg Penner

By comparison ...

• Elmer Layen (1941-46): 5 seasons.
• Bert Bell (1946-59): 14 seasons.
• Pete Rozelle (1960-89): 30 seasons.
• Paul Tagliabue (1989-2006): 18 seasons.
• Roger Goodell (2006-present): 21st season.

supporting_stories.research_notes: NFL owners were notified Saturday that Roger Goodell finalized a 4-year extension through March 31, 2031 per Schefter/Pelissero. Deal is heavily performance-based: 95%+ of total compensation tied to metrics and Compensation Committee discretion per Kraft memo. At the end of this deal, Goodell will be nearly 72 years old and will have served 24 years as commissioner per Schefter. The NFL's CBA with players also expires March 2031 — same timing as Goodell's contract per Schefter. Research: how does Goodell's tenure compare to past commissioners? AlbertBreer provided the comparison: Elmer Layden (5 seasons), Bert Bell (14), Pete Rozelle (30), Paul Tagliabue (18), Goodell (21st season, will hit 24). Rozelle is the gold standard at 30 — Goodell won't match that unless he gets another extension. But 24 years is still second-most in NFL history. What are Goodell's defining moments? Deflategate, the anthem protests, COVID-19 handling, the massive TV deals, international expansion, the Pro Bowl cancellation (literally yesterday per story log Day 2). The timing of the CBA expiring is crucial: Goodell will likely be the guy negotiating the next labor deal, then retiring after it's done. This is a succession-planning move disguised as an extension.

beats.angle: The extension details — 4 years, through March 2031, 24 years total, age 72, heavily performance-based
beats.landing: This is a long-term stability play by the owners, locking in Goodell through the next CBA negotiation

beats.angle: How Goodell's tenure compares to past commissioners and what his legacy will be
beats.landing: Goodell will retire as the second-longest-serving commissioner in NFL history, behind only Rozelle

tweets.text: Gerrit Cole is the only pitcher in MLB history to allow back-to-back-to-back home runs to the first three batters of a game more than once in a career

supporting_stories.research_notes: Fernando Tatis Jr., Jake Cronenworth, and a third batter hit back-to-back-to-back home runs off Gerrit Cole to open the game per TalkinBaseball. Cole is now the ONLY pitcher in MLB history to allow back-to-back-to-back home runs to the first three batters of a game MORE THAN ONCE in a career per TalkinBaseball. This is a Hall of Fame lowlight. Yankees lost 5-1 per ground truth. Research: when was the first time Cole allowed 1-2-3 homers? What are the other instances of back-to-back-to-back homers to open a game in MLB history? How rare is this? Cole is an ace, a Cy Young winner, a $324M man — and he's now the answer to the most embarrassing trivia question in baseball. The Padres are surging, the Yankees are scuffling, and Cole is the poster child for New York's struggles. Compare this to other historic meltdowns: the 2004 ALCS, the 2019 World Series Game 7, etc. This is the kind of thing that defines a season.

beats.angle: The back-to-back-to-back homers to open the game and Cole's historic dubious record
